## Diverging Signals
- **Credit says calm, price says stress.** HY OAS (3.20%) and IG OAS (0.89%) are both inside their lines. At the same time NDX is 10.9% under its high, VXN is 29.38 and VIX is back over 20. Credit is not confirming the equity selloff. That tension usually means the stress is concentrated in tech and AI-linked names, not in the wider financial system. It could also mean credit is lagging.
- **Calm term shape versus rising vol of vol.** VIX/VIX3M is 0.933 (contango), yet VVIX rose to 101.53 and SKEW is 147.14. Traders are not panicking about the near term, but they are paying up for crash protection.
- **Rising yields versus easing spreads.** The 10Y rose to 5.154% while credit spreads tightened. Higher yields are pressuring long-duration tech, and the 2Y at 4.86% shows rate-cut hopes still fading.

## TQQQ Read
- Momentum: **Neutral** (RSI 38.4, between 30 and 70). It is leaning toward oversold but is not there. The stabilizing-after-a-flush setup is not present, and the last two days were both red. Premium is not rich against realized movement (see below).
- Market structure: **DOWNTURN.** Spot is 21.45% under the $73.43 4-week high ($57.68 / $73.43 = 0.7855), past the 20% line. VXN is 29.38, past the 25 line. Both legs are met. Spot is 14.8% above the 4-week low, short of the 30% line for RALLY. The label would flip back to SIDEWAYS on a close above about $58.74 (0.8 × $73.43), which is only 1.8% above spot, so it is fragile.
- Trend: below the 50DMA by 18.67% and below the 200DMA by 12.0%. Spot is 34.24% under the 52-week high and 55.2% above the 52-week low.
- Volatility & premium environment: VXN is 29.38, up 2.91%. Chain ATM IV is 0.75 and IV/HV is 0.73 (HV20 103.9%). IV/HV under 1 means options cost less than the stock has actually been moving, so sellers get no extra cushion. Premium is large in dollars, but swings are large too. Chain IV of 75% is about 15% under the ~88% implied by the 3x-VXN rule of thumb, which is itself only an estimate.
- Put-selling context: HOSTILE. The stage is 5, six of seven lenses are bearish, spot is under both moving averages, TQQQ just fell 3.67% in one day, and the news engine reads SHOCK on tariff and AI-selloff headlines. IV/HV of 0.73 means premium is cheap relative to realized movement. Credit being inside both lines is the one softening sign. A close above the 200DMA near $65.55 with VIX back under 20 would be the first real change. Context only — no strikes, expiries or sizes.
